tool_message: changed callable pipe_converter is passed as a value

reader_a.label: real_omission
reader_a.rationale: The commit changed pipe_converter to (val, inst, field) and at this line wrapped it as `Converter(pipe_converter, takes_self=True, takes_field=True)`. At that commit Converter had no __call__, so pipe() stopped returning a callable. setters.convert still called `c(new_value)`, which breaks the default on_setattr for define with a pipe/list converter, and converters.optional(pipe(...)) also breaks. Upstream fixed this in 6fda0a4 (#1328, 'fix converters.pipe': adds Converter.__call__ and changes setters.convert), e21793e (#1372), and 1e07f46 (#1380), which rewrote this exact return. The checker's stated relation, passing the changed callable as a value, is only roughly the defect mechanism, hence medium confidence.

reader_b.rationale: The site is return Converter(pipe_converter, takes_self=True, takes_field=True). The flags match the new (val, inst, field) arity, so the binding itself is consistent. The defect sits mainly in the body and in callers rather than this binding, so I chose review_worthy over real_omission (conservative).
